content:
ana: Heads-up — we've seen a few incidents where routing for resident-tenants becomes stale after an active/active reconfigure. User requests get routed to a decommissioned primary and stall; traffic doesn't fail over for ~30s. Anyone else noticed this pattern?

matt: haven't seen the full repro, can you paste the steps/logs?

ana: repro steps: 1) start a tenant in region-a, 2) fail over region-a -> region-b via planner, 3) planner flips preferred-region but some proxies keep routing to old leader until their route lease TTL expires. snippet from proxy log: ```WARN route_lookup: lease_missing tenant=acct-42 route_id=rt-7 expected=region-a fallback=region-b```

raj: sounds like lease TTL + cache eviction race. two immediate options: reduce TTL (faster convergence) or add an async reconciliation that pulls planner state and invalidates stale routes proactively. tradeoffs: TTL reduction increases control-plane load, reconciliation adds complexity but can be targeted.

leah: important constraint: can't silently reassign residents in a way that violates data residency. If tenant is bound to EU, any auto-reconcile must ensure the chosen region still satisfies residency. We need a policy layer: auto-reconcile allowed only when target region in same residency set, else fall back to escalation / block.

dmitry: agree. proposal: store a small per-route metadata blob: {preferred_region, residency_tag, epoch, seq}. When planner moves epoch++, reconciliation only accepts updates with epoch >= current. pseudo logic: ```if route.epoch < planner.epoch and candidate.residency==route.residency then invalidate_cache(route) else mark_stale_and_alert(route)``` This keeps us from silently violating residency.

ana: good. what about latency/throughput impact of reconciliation? spikes if we invalidate many routes at once. can we stagger or queue?

infra-bot: scheduled: route-reconcile-canary run starting in 15m across us-west-2 staging. job-id: reconcile-2026-1995

matt: staggered reconcile + write-ahead audit should help. algorithm: per-tenant exponential backoff with jitter, limit concurrent invalidations per proxy to N. also emit metric: stale_route_count and reconcile_duration.

raj: addendum: need idempotent actions and a reconciliation audit log so we can backfill or rollback if planner flaps. store entries like: "action_id, tenant, from_region, to_region, epoch, timestamp, actor". makes debugging and postmortem much easier.

leah: also add a residency-safe fallback mode: if we can't reconcile to a compliant region, we should route to a read-only standby (if available) and surface a clear 409 / residency_error to clients. avoid silent degradation.

ana: action items: (1) raj/infra to prototype reconcile job + audit log with per-tenant rate limits, (2) dmitry to draft small route metadata extension and state-machine pseudocode, (3) leah to write residency policy mapping and failure modes, (4) matt to add metrics/tracing hooks. I'll own the canary run and checklist.

deploy-bot: canary: reconcile-2026-1995 started on staging, monitor /metrics/reconcile.*

ana: thanks all — let's sync in tomorrow's arch slot if prototypes look good. :thumbsup:
